summary.text: A 49-year-old woman was admitted directly to the ICU from another institution after a silent myocardial infarction, possibly in the previous 7 days, complicated by papillary muscle rupture with severe mitral regurgitation. She was mechanically ventilated, in cardiogenic shock with cold, clammy skin, anuria, elevated creatinine, serum lactate 6 mmol/l and LVEF 30% on transthoracic echocardiography.

Transesophageal echocardiography confirmed posterior papillary muscle rupture with severe mitral regurgitation and severe left ventricular dysfunction, and coronary angiography showed triple-vessel coronary artery disease. Given high mortality risk, the Heart Team chose initial stabilization with surgery planned in the same hospitalization.

An IABP, levosimendan and CRRT with hemodiafiltration were used, and cardiogenic shock remitted after 24 hours with improved renal function. Surgical treatment took place on ICU day 5 while she was still on IABP; a triple coronary bypass and mitral valve replacement were performed. Postoperatively, refractory cardiogenic shock developed, and veno-arterial ECMO with IABP was used for 9 days without ECMO-related complications.

Weaning was successful on postoperative day 10, the patient was extubated on postoperative day 12, and the IABP was removed 2 days later. TEE after weaning showed LVEF 40%, normal RV and adequate mechanical mitral valve function. She moved to the ward on postoperative day 20 and was discharged home 1 week later in good condition.
